headline: Structure-conditioned learned models guide peptide, antibody and ligand design
label: Learned Models For Molecular Prediction
summary: Recent preprints couple structure prediction and ensemble sampling with generative design, scoring, and experimental or MD verification.
synthesis: The common thread is predictors that take structural or interaction information as input and feed design, screening, or validation loops. FlexEvo adapts designed binders from one target conformation to alternative conformations at inference, and MIMOSA constrains diffusion-based antibody design to reproduce a cognate binder interface via natural interaction fingerprints. Kryptix-1 pairs conformational ensembles with consensus pocket scoring, reporting 80% success on 10 CryptoBench proteins versus 20% for a static baseline. Boltz2-Notebook wraps Boltz-2 structure and affinity prediction with a benchmark of 317 BindingDB pairs, while AnewDDE links structure prediction, affinity estimation, design, and LLM-based ADMET reasoning in a closed loop. Mirror-Score adds calibrated, inference-only scoring for D-peptide/L-protein complexes, exposing limits of sequence-compatibility ranking. The new element is explicit coupling of learned predictors to conformational ensembles and calibrated scoring, though the set is heterogeneous and includes physics-based MMPBSA and PepSpace workflows.
